diagnostics.title: Usage tap: unknown ingress protocol for a same-protocol 2xx body
diagnostics.summary: The usage tap could not recognize the ingress protocol of a same-protocol 2xx body, so it bills 0 tokens for the request. Warned once per (protocol, reason); BILLING_TAP_DECODE_FAIL_TOTAL carries the volume.
diagnostics.action: None if the protocol is genuinely unmetered. If a metered dialect is billing 0 tokens, the protocol name is unexpected — check the route configuration and for a busbar update covering it.

diagnostics.title: Usage tap: failed to parse a same-protocol 2xx body as JSON
diagnostics.summary: The usage tap could not parse a same-protocol 2xx body as JSON, so it bills 0 tokens for the request. Warned once per (protocol, reason); the raw body is never logged (it may carry secrets). BILLING_TAP_DECODE_FAIL_TOTAL carries the volume.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals per request. Sustained occurrence for one upstream means it is returning non-JSON 2xx bodies busbar cannot meter; investigate that upstream.

diagnostics.title: Event-stream :event-type header exceeds the string cap (frame dropped)
diagnostics.summary: An event-stream `:event-type` header exceeded the AWS type-7 string cap, so busbar dropped the frame rather than emit a malformed one. This is unreachable for any real upstream event name (the only caller-supplied value on the frame); it guards the data path and fires per-frame, so it is emitted at debug.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals per frame; a real upstream event name never trips it. Sustained occurrence would mean a caller is supplying an over-long event-type, worth checking the ingress path.

diagnostics.title: Event-stream :exception-type header exceeds the string cap (frame dropped)
diagnostics.summary: An event-stream `:exception-type` header exceeded the AWS type-7 string cap, so busbar dropped the exception frame — a swallowed mid-stream error signal — rather than emit a malformed one. It fires per-frame on the streaming data path and is near-unreachable for a real exception type, so it is emitted at debug.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals per frame. If it recurs, an upstream mid-stream error carried an over-long exception-type name; check the egress dialect mapping for that upstream.

diagnostics.title: Event-stream frame exceeds MAX_FRAME_BYTES (frame dropped)
diagnostics.summary: An event-stream frame's total size exceeded MAX_FRAME_BYTES, so busbar dropped it rather than byte-truncate the payload (a truncated JSON body is worse for a native SDK than no frame). Unreachable for any real upstream event-stream delta; it only guards a pathological multi-MiB single event and fires per-frame, so it is emitted at debug.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals per frame; dropping is graceful (nothing is emitted for that event). Sustained occurrence would indicate an upstream emitting abnormally large single events, worth investigating that lane.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode clamped n>1 to 1
diagnostics.summary: On a cross-protocol hop the neutral response IR carries a single candidate, so a request asking for n>1 completions is clamped to n=1 before the egress writer emits it — otherwise extra choices would be generated, billed, and then dropped. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. To use n>1, route the request to a same-protocol lane where the body is forwarded verbatim.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped a reasoning/thinking ask
diagnostics.summary: A request's reasoning/thinking parameter was dropped on the cross-protocol seam because the target lane does not declare the reasoning capability; the request proceeds at the backend's default thinking level. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Set `reasoning: true` on the model or pool member if the backend accepts thinking params.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped prompt-cache breakpoints
diagnostics.summary: Prompt-cache breakpoints were cleared on the cross-protocol seam because the target lane's dialect gates its cache marker per model and the lane does not declare the capability; the request proceeds uncached. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Set `prompt_caching: true` on the model if the backend accepts cache markers.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped cache_control breakpoints past the dialect cap
diagnostics.summary: The request carried more cache_control breakpoints than the egress dialect allows (the target vendor 400s past its documented cap), so the breakpoints past the cap were dropped before the writer emitted them. Reachable only cross-protocol. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Reduce the number of cache breakpoints, or route to a same-protocol lane if the full set is load-bearing.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped hosted (built-in) tools
diagnostics.summary: One or more provider-hosted (built-in) tools were dropped on the cross-protocol seam because they have no function-tool equivalent on a backend that does not host them; forwarding them would emit a malformed empty-name function tool the upstream rejects. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Route hosted-tool requests to a lane whose backend hosts them.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped per-message participant names (messages[].name)
diagnostics.summary: Per-message participant names (`messages[].name`) were dropped on the cross-protocol seam because no target protocol models a per-message speaker name, so a multi-speaker transcript reaches the backend with its speaker labels removed. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Put the speaker in the message text, or route to a same-protocol lane that models them.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped a provider cachedContent reference
diagnostics.summary: A provider `cachedContent` reference was dropped on the cross-protocol seam because the referenced context cache lives server-side at the origin provider and cannot be projected into `contents`: the backend answers on the visible history only and the caller is billed full uncached input. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Route cachedContent requests to a same-protocol lane to use the cache.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped an unmapped member
diagnostics.summary: A member of the source dialect that the target dialect has no form for was dropped on the cross-protocol seam: a request member its map file does not model, or a request or answer content block of a kind the other dialect cannot carry. Nothing is put in its place. Only the wire path is logged (never the value). Warned on every translated request or response it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`); a request-side drop is also recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Route to a same-protocol lane (which forwards the caller's original bytes verbatim) if a named field is load-bearing.

diagnostics.title: Stop sequences truncated to the protocol's documented cap
diagnostics.summary: The request carried more stop sequences than the target protocol's documented cap allows, so the excess were dropped before forwarding. Warned on every translated request it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), and recorded in the audit log as `egress.control_unrepresentable` naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. Reduce the number of stop sequences, or route to a same-protocol lane if the full set is required.

diagnostics.title: Cross-protocol transcode dropped response-side provider metadata
diagnostics.summary: Response-side provider metadata (a vendor guardrail `trace`, a vendor `safetyRatings`) was dropped on the cross-protocol seam because it is a vendor-scoped artifact the caller's protocol has no shape to receive. Warned on every translated response it affects (one drop path, `codec::drops`), naming the wire path.
diagnostics.action: None — self-heals. If this metadata is compliance evidence, route the request to a same-protocol lane where the upstream body reaches the client verbatim.
